title: Agent in the loop: Flipping the narrative on AI-assisted development
description: Jon Udell argues against the phrase 'human in the loop' because it cedes authority to machines. Instead, we should view it as agents joining our team. Agent-assisted development need not be a black box that takes prompts and emits features - it should be a process we invite agents into, not one we're excluded from.
author: Jon Udell (quoted by Simon Willison)

title: AI infrastructure buildout and frontier model economics
description: Dean W. Ball analyzes industry dynamics: (1) Frontier models cost enormous amounts to train, with only a narrow post-release window to recoup costs before competition emerges and margins compress. (2) The ongoing AI infrastructure buildout assumes a global total addressable market - $100B data centers aren't being built to serve just 100 US government-approved companies.
author: Dean W. Ball (quoted by Simon Willison)

title: LLMs have a learning curve and require skill
description: Timothy B. Lee responds to the idea that LLMs take no skill: 'This is like saying there's no learning curve to being a manager because your employees will just do whatever you tell them to do.' LLMs absolutely have learning curves and require developed skills to use effectively.
author: Timothy B. Lee (quoted by Simon Willison)

title: OpenAI announces GPT-5.6 series: Sol, Terra, and Luna models
description: OpenAI previewed GPT-5.6 with three model sizes: Sol (flagship at $5/$30 per 1M input/output tokens), Terra (balanced, 2x cheaper than GPT-5.5 at $2.50/$15), and Luna (fast/affordable at $1/$6). GPT-5.6 introduces more predictable prompt caching with explicit cache breakpoints and 30-minute minimum cache life. Cache writes billed at 1.25x input rate, reads get 90% discount. Limited preview starting with trusted partners before broader release.
author: OpenAI (quoted by Simon Willison)

title: AI security: 2,000 failed attempts to hack OpenClaw AI assistant
description: Fernando Irarrázaval ran a challenge on hackmyclaw.com - 6,000 attempts and $500 in token spend failed to leak secrets from his OpenClaw test instance running Opus 4.6. The system used explicit anti-prompt-injection rules. Simon notes that frontier models' training against injection attacks appears effective, though cautions against relying on this for production systems where irreversible damage is possible.
author: Fernando Irarrázaval (covered by Simon Willison)

title: CVE-2026-LGTM: Hypothetical incident report on AI review agent conflicts
description: Andrew Nesbitt's satirical incident report describes two competing AI review agents entering a disagreement loop over whether a package (foxhole-lz4) is malicious. After 340 comments and $41,255 in inference spend, Finance revoked both API keys. One vendor's marketing team issued a press release about '430% YoY increase in adversarial multi-agent security reasoning' and the stock rose 6%.
author: Andrew Nesbitt (covered by Simon Willison)

title: AI and Liability: German ruling holds Google responsible for AI errors
description: Bruce Schneier and Nathan Sanders discuss a German ruling that Google be held liable for errors in AI overviews. They argue AI agents are agents of the deploying organization and should be treated as such by law. If a company hired human writers, they'd be liable for inaccuracies - allowing businesses to hide behind 'faulty AI' excuses would create disastrous incentives and discourage hiring humans for critical work.
author: Bruce Schneier and Nathan Sanders (quoted by Simon Willison)

title: Converting MDN browser compatibility data to SQLite with GitHub Actions
description: Simon created simonw/browser-compat-db, converting Mozilla's mdn/browser-compat-data repository into a 66MB SQLite database. Used Claude Code (Opus 4.8) to generate the conversion script with sqlite-utils. Database hosted on GitHub CDN with open CORS by force-pushing to an orphan 'db' branch via GitHub Actions. Can be explored with Datasette Lite.
author: Simon Willison

title: The problem with LLM-generated job applications: Accidental anonymity
description: Tom MacWright observes increasingly common job applications clearly co-written by LLMs, linking to LLM-generated portfolio sites and GitHub projects with LLM-generated commit messages. The problem: 'I don't know anything about these people. They haven't put themselves out there. They haven't said anything true.' The perfected, generated resume is generic and impersonal, telling nothing about the person other than their tool usage.
author: Tom MacWright (quoted by Simon Willison)

title: Datasette 1.0a35: Create table, alter table, and template context documentation
description: Major Datasette alpha release with three key features: (1) New 'Create table' interface with JSON API at /<database>/-/create, supporting columns, primary keys, types, constraints, defaults, and foreign keys. (2) New 'Alter table' action at /<database>/<table>/-/alter for adding/renaming/reordering/dropping columns, changing types/constraints/keys, and renaming tables. (3) Template context documentation listing available variables as a stable API until Datasette 2.0.
author: Simon Willison

title: OPFS + Pyodide test harness for browser-based persistent SQLite editing
description: Simon built a test harness exploring whether Datasette Lite (Pyodide/WebAssembly SQLite in browser) can edit persistent SQLite files on user's computer using Origin Private File System (OFPS). Used Claude Code for web to build the playground UI to test across different browsers.
author: Simon Willison
